item.title: As energy demand surges, Southeast Asia faces an uncomfortable nuclear question
item.description: Long treated in Southeast Asia as a distant possibility, nuclear power is quietly returning to regional policy discussions, as the risks of energy shortfalls, price instability and system fragility are becoming harder to ignore.

item.title: Tourists become less environmentally responsible when in ‘holiday mode’, study finds
item.description: Research from University of Queensland shows that travellers’ core values may remain intact, but a “vacation place identity” makes people feel freer and less accountable for their behaviour while away from home.

item.title: Inside China’s solar villages
item.description: For a decade, solar power has been bringing opportunities to China’s villages. What does that mean today?

item.title: Analysis: Clean energy drove more than a third of China’s GDP growth in 2025
item.description: Solar power, electric vehicles (EVs) and other clean-energy technologies drove more than a third of the growth in China’s economy in 2025 – and more than 90 per cent of the rise in investment.

item.title: Taiwan delays 20 per cent renewables target beyond 2026 as tighter solar rules slow rollout
item.description: The government shifts focus to rooftop solar and offshore wind, says power supply will remain stable despite regulatory curbs and nuclear restart uncertainty.

item.title: Chile’s Julio Cordano elected chair of UN plastic pollution treaty talks
item.description: The position had been vacant for four months amid a deadlock in negotiations for the treaty to curb global plastic pollution.

item.title: A river becomes a channel for cross-border pollution from Nepal to India
item.description: The Sirsiya River, once central to daily life, agriculture, and religious rituals in southern Nepal, is now heavily polluted with industrial waste and sewage, rendering it a public health hazard.

item.title: Climate enforcement weak in India-EU ‘mother of all deals’, experts say
item.description: Climate policy experts reflect on the agreement’s focus on “cooperation”, “dialogue” for environmental matters in lieu of binding targets.

item.title: IPBES: Four key takeaways on how nature loss threatens the global economy
item.description: The “undervaluing” of nature by businesses is fuelling its decline and putting the global economy at risk, according to a major new report.

item.title: Can Moscow and Seoul help Vietnam achieve its nuclear energy ambitions?
item.description: Vietnam has grand plans to build a series of nuclear power plants. But it faces several challenges.
